config.info: Complete the following problems using {!GRI|これ, それ, or あれ|l2-p1}.
config.quizlet:
Translate the sentences into Japanese.

This is my pen.
{これはわたしのペンです|これは私のペンです|answer}。
That is Ken's book.
{それはけんさんのほんです|それはけんさんの本です|answer}。
What is that? *points to a building in the distance*
{あれはなんですか|あれは何ですか|answer}。
Is this meat?
{これはにくですか|これは肉ですか|answer}。

Mary and Takeshi are talking. Fill in the blanks with これ, それ, or あれ.

メアリー：{これ}はたけしさんのかさですか。(Mary is holding an umbrella)
たけし：いいえ、{それ}はみちこさんのかさです。

{これ}はメアリーさんのさいふですか。(Takeshi is holding a wallet)
メアリー：ええ、わたしのさいふです。

たけしさん、{あれ}はたけしさんのじてんしゃですか。(Mary points to a bike in the distance)

たけし：ええ、そうです。

メアリー：{あれ}はなんですか。(Mary points to a building in the distance)

たけし：ゆうびんきょくです。

delivery.beat: Aakash and Tom place the source objects between their desks so これ・それ・あれ keeps its original distance contrast.

steps.evidence: Watch classmates identify objects on the table and say whose they are.

steps.form: これは N です。これは N の N です。
steps.meaning: Identify an object and say who it belongs to.
steps.contrast: これ is the object by the speaker; それ is the object by the listener.
steps.workedExample: これは ジョディさんの ほんです。

steps.activity: Listen for the object and owner, then choose the matching これ／それ sentence.

feedback.error: If the owner and object are reversed, の changes whose thing is being described.
feedback.retry: Read the phrase as 'owner's object' and try the noun order again.

progressiveHints: Hold up one nearby item and use これは.
Add わたしの before the item if it is yours.

feedback.error: If これ and それ do not match the object's distance, or の has no following noun, the meaning changes.
feedback.retry: Point again, choose the correct demonstrative, and repeat the one sentence.

progressiveHints: Choose two objects, one near you and one near another person.
Use これは／それは N です and add N の N once.

feedback.error: If a sentence lacks です or a demonstrative is used without an object statement, the reader cannot identify the item.
feedback.retry: Check each line has a pointer, a noun, and an ending, then rewrite the incomplete line.

learningObjectives: Say who you are with 〜は 〜です, and ask a yes/no question with か.
Add 'me too' with も, and say what belongs to whom with の (わたしの かさ).
Point at things near you, near a friend, and far away: これ・それ・あれ.
Ask これは なんですか and agree with そうです.
Read and hand-write your first four kanji: 一, 二, 三, 人.

lines.japanese: こんばんは。にほんごの クラスへ ようこそ。わたしは リエです。
lines.reading: こんばんは。にほんごの クラスへ ようこそ。わたしは リエです。
lines.english: Good evening. Welcome to the Japanese class. I'm Rie.
lines.note: The very first 〜は 〜です of the whole course.

lines.japanese: はじめまして。ヘンリーです。どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。
lines.reading: はじめまして。ヘンリーです。どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。
lines.english: Nice to meet you. I'm Henry. I look forward to working with you.
lines.note: The set greeting you'll say a hundred times.

lines.japanese: あのう、リエさん。これは にほんごで なんですか。
lines.reading: あのう、リエさん。これは にほんごで なんですか。
lines.english: Um, Rie — what's this called in Japanese?
lines.note: これ = the thing in Tom's own hand.

lines.japanese: それは「キーホルダー」ですよ。トムさんの ですか。
lines.reading: それは「キーホルダー」ですよ。トムさんの ですか。
lines.english: That's a 'keychain'. Is it yours, Tom?
lines.note: それ = near you (the listener); トムさんの = Tom's (の).

lines.japanese: じゃあ、あれも キーホルダーですか。
lines.reading: じゃあ、あれも キーホルダーですか。
lines.english: Then is that one over there a keychain too?
lines.note: あれ = far from both of us; も = too.

lines.japanese: そうです。きょうは「これ・それ・あれ」を れんしゅうしましょう。
lines.reading: そうです。きょうは「これ・それ・あれ」を れんしゅうしましょう。
lines.english: That's right. Tonight let's practise 'this, that, and that over there'.
lines.note: そうです confirms; Rie names the lesson without any fuss.

explanation.recap: Over the last few weeks you learned to read and write the kana — every あ, か, さ, and their little brothers な, は, ば, ぱ. Tonight those characters stop being a chart and become the first words you can actually say out loud.
explanation.intro: Everything tonight is one small copula: です, a gentle 'is'. With it you can say who you are (わたしは 〜です), ask a yes/no question (〜ですか), point at the things around you (これ・それ・あれ), and say whose they are (わたしの 〜). Four moves — and suddenly you can hold a first conversation.

grammarPoints.meaning: A is B — saying who or what something is; か turns it into a question; も means 'also'
grammarPoints.explanation: は marks the topic — the thing you're talking about — and です is a soft 'is/am/are'. わたしは ヘンリーです = 'I'm Henry'. Add か to the very end to make a yes/no question: ヘンリーさんは がくせいですか = 'Are you a student, Henry?' To say 'also / too', swap は for も: わたしも がくせいです = 'I'm a student too'. Answer yes/no with はい / いいえ.
grammarPoints.watchFor: The topic particle は is written は but pronounced 'wa'. も takes the place of は — you never say もは.
grammarPoints.commonError: Dropping です (わたしは ヘンリー on its own sounds unfinished), or keeping は when you mean 'too' (say わたしも, not わたしはも).

examples.reading: わたしは リエです。

examples.ja: ヘンリーさんは がくせいですか。…はい、がくせいです。
examples.reading: ヘンリーさんは がくせいですか。…はい、がくせいです。
examples.en: Are you a student, Henry? …Yes, I am.
examples.note: か makes the question; はい answers it.

examples.ja: わたしも がくせいです。
examples.reading: わたしも がくせいです。

grammarPoints.pattern: これ・それ・あれ ／ この・その・あの＋N（＋ そうです）
grammarPoints.nameJa: これは なんですか
grammarPoints.meaning: this / that / that over there — pointing at things and asking what they are
grammarPoints.explanation: これ is near me, それ is near you, あれ is over there away from both of us. These three stand alone: これは ほんです = 'this is a book'. When you want to attach the pointer to a noun, use この・その・あの instead, and they always need a noun right after: この ほん = 'this book'. Ask what something is with これは なんですか. Agree with そうです ('that's right'); show mild surprise with そうですか ('oh, really?').
grammarPoints.watchFor: これ・それ・あれ stand alone; この・その・あの can never stand alone — always この＋noun.
grammarPoints.commonError: Saying この on its own for 'this one', or これ ほん with no は. Use これは for 'this is…', and この ほん for 'this book'.

examples.ja: それは なんですか。…とけいです。
examples.reading: それは なんですか。…とけいです。
examples.note: それ = near the listener; なんですか asks 'what?'.

examples.ja: あの かばんは トムさんのですか。…そうです。
examples.reading: あの かばんは トムさんのですか。…そうです。
examples.en: Is that bag over there Tom's? …That's right.
examples.note: あの＋noun; そうです confirms.

grammarPoints.meaning: の joins two nouns: 'my umbrella', 'the teacher's watch', 'a Japanese book'
grammarPoints.explanation: Put の between two nouns and the first one describes the second — usually 'whose' or 'which kind'. わたしの かさ = 'my umbrella'. せんせいの とけい = 'the teacher's watch'. にほんごの ほん = 'a Japanese-language book'. Ask 'whose?' with だれの: これは だれの かばんですか = 'whose bag is this?'
grammarPoints.watchFor: Order is owner/describer + の + thing. The thing you're talking about comes last.
grammarPoints.commonError: Reversing it to かさの わたし. It's always わたしの かさ — 'me's umbrella'.

examples.ja: これは わたしの かばんです。
examples.reading: これは わたしの かばんです。

examples.ja: それは だれの かさですか。
examples.reading: それは だれの かさですか。

label.en: Uses これは / それは 〜です correctly

title.ja: はじめての かんじ

provenance.note: First-kanji set (numbers plus 'person') chosen for absolute-beginner handwriting; supports the Level 1 script strand. Character list is an original selection, not a copied source sheet.

handwriting.mnemonic: A single flat line — one stroke, drawn left to right. That's 'one'.
handwriting.tracePrompt: Trace 一 once, then write it twice from memory.

handwriting.mnemonic: Two lines, the top one shorter: count them for 'two'.
handwriting.tracePrompt: Trace 二, then write 二つ (ふたつ) from memory.

handwriting.mnemonic: Three stacked lines — one, two, three. The middle one is shortest.
handwriting.tracePrompt: Trace 三, then write 三つ (みっつ) from memory.

handwriting.mnemonic: Two legs caught mid-step — a person walking.
handwriting.tracePrompt: Trace 人, then write あの人 (that person) from memory.

prompt.ja: 「ひと」の かんじは どれですか。

exercises.explanation: 人 (ひと / ジン・ニン) is 'person' — two legs mid-step. 一 and 三 are numbers.

wrongAnswerExplanations.message: 一 is a single flat line — that's 'one', not 'person'.
三 is three stacked lines — that's 'three'. 'Person' is 人.

exercises.explanation: 三 has three lines — it's 'three' (さん / みっつ).

wrongAnswerExplanations.message: 'One' is 一 — a single line. 三 has three lines.
'Two' is 二 — two lines. Count the lines in 三: there are three.

provenance.note: Original spiral review folding in the earlier Level 1 weeks (kana and first greetings).

prompt.en: In わたしは がくせいです, how is は read here?
prompt.ja: 「わたしは がくせいです」の は の よみかたは？

exercises.explanation: As the topic particle, は is pronounced 'wa', even though it's written は.

wrongAnswerExplanations.message: The character is は, but as the topic particle it's read 'wa', not 'ha'.
It's not 'a' — the topic particle は is pronounced 'wa'.

prompt.en: Match each greeting to when you use it.
prompt.ja: あいさつと ばめんを あわせましょう。

exercises.explanation: はじめまして opens a first meeting; どうぞ よろしく closes an introduction; こんばんは is an evening hello; ありがとうございます is thanks.

right.en: meeting someone for the first time

left.ja: どうぞ よろしく おねがいします
ありがとうございます

mission.title: Show and tell
mission.prompt: Tom goes first, holding up his keychain. Everyone takes a turn: say はじめまして and your name, hold up one small thing that's yours and say これは わたしの 〜です, then ask one classmate それは なんですか about theirs.
successCriteria: You name your own object with これは わたしの 〜です, using の.
You ask a classmate それは なんですか about their thing.
You close warmly with どうぞ よろしく おねがいします.

modelAnswer.ja: はじめまして。アアカシュです。これは わたしの かぎです。トムさん、それは なんですか。どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。
modelAnswer.reading: はじめまして。アアカシュです。これは わたしの かぎです。トムさん、それは なんですか。どうぞ よろしく おねがいします。
modelAnswer.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Aakash. This is my key. Tom, what's that (in your hand)? I look forward to working with you.

label.en: Names an object with の correctly
Asks それは なんですか to a classmate

extracted.back: A is B — say who or what something is (topic は read 'wa')
this (near me) / that (near you) / that over there
の joins two nouns: わたしの かさ = my umbrella
one — イチ / ひと-つ (一つ)
two — ニ / ふた-つ (二つ)
three — サン / みっ-つ (三つ)
person — ジン・ニン / ひと (あの人)
